record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: For given distributions, can one design effective algorithms to decide whether they are jointly mixable or to solve the minimax assignment problem from Section 1? In particular, under what conditions do the swapping algorithms discussed in the paper converge?

evidence.quote: 1. Algorithms to determine whether some distributions are jointly mixable, or solving question (1) in Section 1: see for instance [28, 12, 34, 19]. The conditions under which the swapping algorithms in [28] converges are still unclear.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $F_1,\dots,F_d$ be one-dimensional probability distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$ with finite means. The tuple $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$ is called jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_1,\dots,X_d$ on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim F_i$ for each $i$, such that
$$ X_1+X_2+\cdots+X_d = c \quad \text{almost surely} $$
for some constant $c\in\mathbb{R}$ (necessarily $c=\sum_i \mathbb{E}[X_i]$). When $d=1$ and a single distribution $F$ admits such a representation with $d$ i.i.d. copies summing to a constant, $F$ is called $d$-completely mixable.

Discrete approximation. Given $F_1,\dots,F_d$, fix a large integer $N$ and form a $d\times N$ matrix $M$ whose $i$-th row consists of $N$ quantiles $F_i^{-1}((j-1/2)/N)$, $j=1,\dots,N$. A swapping (rearrangement) algorithm iteratively rearranges entries within each row of $M$ to minimize the variance of the column sums; convergence here means that the column-sum variance tends to $0$ as $N\to\infty$ and the iteration count grows.

Problem. 
(a) Design an effective algorithm that, given $F_1,\dots,F_d$ (specified e.g. by their quantile functions to arbitrary precision), decides whether $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$ is jointly mixable.
(b) Design an effective algorithm to solve the minimax assignment problem
$$ \min_{\sigma_2,\dots,\sigma_d \in S_N} \;\max_{1\le j\le N}\; \Big( x_{1,j}+\sum_{i=2}^{d} x_{i,\sigma_i(j)} \Big) - \min_{1\le j\le N}\Big(x_{1,j}+\sum_{i=2}^{d} x_{i,\sigma_i(j)}\Big), $$
where $(x_{i,j})$ is the matrix $M$ above and $S_N$ is the symmetric group on $N$ elements; equivalently, find permutations of the rows that minimize the range of the column sums.
(c) Identify explicit, sharp sufficient conditions on $F_1,\dots,F_d$ under which the swapping (rearrangement) algorithm — which at each step replaces the entries of one row by a permutation that makes that row oppositely ordered to the sum of the remaining rows — converges to an arrangement whose column sums have variance $0$ (in the limit $N\to\infty$).
artifact.status_search_result: Detection of joint/complete mixability and the worst-VaR rearrangement problem have been studied by Puccetti–Wang ("Detecting complete and joint mixability", 2015) and refined by Block Rearrangement Algorithm variants (Bernard–McLeish, Boudt et al., 2017+). Convergence rate results for the minimal-variance problem and partial guarantees for BRA exist, but general necessary-and-sufficient convergence conditions for the original swapping/rearrangement algorithm remain not fully characterized; thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Detecting complete and joint mixability
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm to detect whether given marginals are jointly mixable, based on rearrangement.
status_evidence.claim: Provides algorithmic detection of joint mixability, addressing part (a) partially.

status_evidence.title: Rearrangement algorithm and maximum entropy (Bernard et al., Ann Oper Res 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Block Rearrangement Algorithm generalizes RA, with convergence-rate results for the minimal variance problem.
status_evidence.claim: Partial convergence-rate results for swapping/rearrangement algorithms exist, but full convergence conditions are not established.

status_evidence.title: Implementing the Rearrangement Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses practical convergence behavior of RA and BRA.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence is studied empirically and partially theoretically, indicating ongoing work.
